slides.0.title: The AOG system
slides.0.subtitle: Appellation d'Origine Garantie: stricter than you might expect
slides.1.title: The legal framework
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Two founding texts
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Decree 2-75-321 of 12 August 1977 covers vinification, holding, circulation and trade; Order 869-75 of 15 August 1977 covers the appellation regime
slides.1.highlights.1.title: AOG and AOC
slides.1.highlights.1.content: AOG is a guaranteed origin covering a larger area. AOC is a controlled origin that must lie within an AOG, with more detailed conditions
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Who is in charge
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The food safety office ONSSA handles label applications, and the commission nationale viti-vinicole gives professional advice
slides.1.content: The system clearly shows French influence, but the details cannot be assumed to match French rules.
slides.2.title: What an AOG requires
slides.2.highlights.0.title: One area
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Wine and grapes must both come from the same delimited area
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Natural 12°
slides.2.highlights.1.content: At least 12° natural alcohol, with any enrichment forbidden
slides.2.highlights.2.title: No irrigation in principle
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Vineyards may not be irrigated unless a ministerial order grants an exception for particular ecological conditions
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Yields set yearly
slides.2.highlights.3.content: AOG yield limits are not fixed: an order sets them each year for each appellation
slides.2.highlights.4.title: Separate vinification and a label
slides.2.highlights.4.content: It must be vinified separately from other wine, meet analytical standards and obtain the appellation label
slides.2.content: Most likely to be asked are the 12° and the ban on enrichment: in hot Morocco the grapes must reach the level on their own.
slides.3.title: Three label sessions a year
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The Primeur session
slides.3.highlights.1.title: The Exceptionnel session
slides.3.highlights.1.content: December to January, opened only on a reasoned request from the trade
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The Pleine saison session
slides.3.highlights.2.content: March to April, when producers submit their remaining eligible wines
slides.3.content: Labels are applied for by batch; registering in a region does not earn one automatically.
